interpretation: Instruction: load the four charge cups from the tray into the atomizer's crucible, standing upright around the sealing rod. Objects found from depth and images. The tray held four light-grey cups, each 19-19.4 mm in diameter and about 70 mm tall, standing in sockets on a 4 cm grid, at A (0.133,-0.181), B (0.173,-0.181), C (0.133,-0.221) and D (0.173,-0.221); perception merged them into fragments (obj1-obj4). The atomizer is the white box obj5 (x 0.2-0.4, y 0-0.2, top at z=0.12) with its lid obj7 open at the back. The crucible sits in the box's square opening. From wrist depth: inner wall radius 28.5 mm, rim at z=0.12, floor at z=0.010. The sealing rod is centred at (0.3002, 0.0990), radius 6.3 mm, top at z=0.1498. That leaves an annulus about 22 mm wide for 19.4 mm cups, so each cup has about 1.3 mm of radial clearance per side. Goal state: all four cups standing upright on the crucible floor in that annulus, spaced around the rod; I planned slots at 0, 90, 180 and 270 deg, at r=17.4 mm. No ambiguity about which objects were meant. Which end of the cups is the top was only clear while they stood on the tray (lighter top face).
plan: Key facts from looking first. (1) Straight-down poses over the crucible are unreachable above TCP z~0.13 (joint5 limit ±1.22), but poses with the approach tilted 35° from vertical (side_pose tilt 55, az 0-30) reach all slots up to z~0.24. (2) The gripper is binary, opening to 7 cm, with chunky jaws (about 34 mm wide, 12 mm thick). On the 4 cm cup grid a fully open jaw clears the neighbours only on certain diagonals and approach directions, so I scored every grasp with my own jaw model against the neighbour cylinders. (3) The arm has a steady-state tracking error of 3-7 mm plus about 2° of orientation that changes with motion direction, so the plan was closed-loop. Per cup: grasp vertical with a tilted (35°) approach, measure the cup axis in the TCP frame by fitting circles to point-cloud slices, and compute a release pose that makes the cup vertical with its bottom centre over the slot. Transfer with the cup bottom kept above the box top and the rod top, then re-measure the cup in the world and correct x/y at a height above the rod top (bottom about 0.162). Descend to a bottom height of about 0.126-0.145 (inside the rod-top level, above the rim), re-measure, and release so the cup slides down the annulus. Pick order D, C, B, A, chosen so each grasp had free space on its jaw side. Changes along the way: after C slipped out in transit I switched to a deeper grasp (TCP 1.45 cm below the cup top instead of 1.35 cm above it) and slower transfers. After A pivoted about 30° in the grip on hitting the rod top, I rotated the gripper about its closing axis to make the cup vertical again (approach 28° below horizontal). I also yawed the gripper -30° to step around a wrist singularity (q5 about 0).

steps.what: Read robot and scene; heightmaps of tray and crucible; wrist look pose (TCP 0.24,0.10,0.22) for wrist depth into the crucible
steps.why: Get exact cup, crucible and rod geometry and reachability before moving
steps.result: Measured cup radius 9.5 mm, tops at z=0.0765; crucible floor 0.010, wall radius 28.5 mm, rod radius 6.3 mm, top 0.1498. Found that straight-down is unreachable above z 0.13 over the crucible. Steps 0-34.

steps.why: Hoped for a partial opening to clear neighbouring cups
steps.result: Gripper is binary: 0.55 closed it fully. Opened again; measured jaw geometry from wrist depth. Steps 34-64.

steps.what: Grasped D with az -45, tilt 55, TCP z 0.09 (1.35 cm above the cup top); flipped yaw to keep joint6 continuous; two-stage descent with error compensation
steps.why: Best clearance to neighbours (8.1 mm measured at the actual pose) of the reachable tilted grasps
steps.result: Grip reading 0.816 (held). Slice regression after lifting showed the cup pivoted 6.3° in the grip. Steps 64-265.

steps.what: Transferred D to slot 270 via a transit waypoint; measured the cup in the world, corrected x/y twice, descended to bottom ~0.133, re-centred to r 17.0 mm, released
steps.why: Tilt-compensated release pose plus closed-loop correction on the measured cup, since tracking and orientation errors moved the cup bottom by up to 6 mm
steps.result: Cup slid in. Wrist depth at the look pose showed its top at z=0.081 at 255-285 deg, so it stands on the floor. Steps 265-513.

steps.what: Grasped C with az -90, flipped, TCP z 0.09 (shallow grip)
steps.why: Large clearance (19.9 mm) once D was gone
steps.result: Held (0.818), but the cup tilted 5.4°, partly along the closing axis. Steps 513-674.

steps.what: Transferred C toward slot 180 (yaw change of about 105°, 5 s)
steps.result: FAILED: grip read 0.998 on arrival. C slipped out in transit and lies on its side on the table at (0.27,-0.074) (obj24). Steps 674-753.

steps.what: Grasped B deeper: az 0, TCP z 0.062, so the jaws cover about 4 cm of the cup
steps.why: A more secure grip after losing C

steps.what: Slow transfer of B to slot 180; aligned above, then low; my check held the first release (top leaning toward the rod); shifted outward 0.7 mm and released at bottom r 16.7 mm
steps.why: Keep the inner edge off the rod and the outer edge inside the rim
steps.result: Wrist depth: B's top at z=0.081 at 165-195 deg, standing on the floor. Steps 957-1225.

steps.what: Grasped A deep (az -30, TCP z 0.062), almost no pivot (1.7°); transferred to slot 0
steps.result: The above-slot fit was noisy (0.74 mm residual). On the 3.6 cm descent the cup's bottom edge hit the rod top: the TCP stalled 17 mm high and the cup pivoted in the grip. My next two corrections chased the extrapolated bottom of the tilted cup and raised its tilt to about 30°. Steps 1225-1602.

steps.what: Recovered A: lifted, then rotated the gripper -30° and later -3.6° and -8.7° about its closing axis (approach about 28° below horizontal) until the cup hung vertical (1-2° tilt)
steps.why: Gravity-hung pivot cannot be undone by gripping; rotating the gripper about the pivot axis restores verticality
steps.result: Worked; both scene crops showed the cup vertical. Along the way two of my own mistakes: a bad bottom estimate (box-top points) raised the cup 3.4 cm, and a stale z command from a refused call later lowered it onto the rim (+10 mm stall, cup tilted 8.8° again). Also a wrist singularity blocked the planner until I yawed -30°. Steps 1602-1912.

steps.what: Aligned A over slot 0 (r 17.7 mm, tilt 1.6°), descended past the rod top in a checked step (z error -4.9 mm = normal sag, no stall), released
steps.result: A is in. Its top at z~0.08 is visible at 315-345 and 15 deg; the rod top hides its middle from the look pose. Three cups in. Steps 1912-2021.

steps.what: Tried to recover C (lying): planned a top-down grasp near its top end, then a rotation to a horizontal approach so it would hang bottom-down
steps.why: The task needs all four cups
steps.result: The straight path from the look pose drove the open jaws onto the box's top edge. My arm check filtered out gripper-link contacts and hid this. The arm stalled and the jaws closed on nothing. I escaped with a tilted pose, but then descended onto C with the jaws still closed (I had not reopened them). Stopped the attempt: a full recovery would not fit the remaining time and risked the placed cups. Steps 2021-2258.

steps.what: Retreated to the look pose; final checks with the wrist, left and right cameras; finish_episode
steps.result: Final: D, B and A upright on the crucible floor around the rod (tops z 0.080-0.081). C lying on the table; tray empty. Episode finished at step 2330 of 4500, about 52 of 70 min.

diagnosis:
The task failed: only 3 of 4 cups are in the crucible. The decisive error was the shallow grasp on cup C. Holding only the top 1.7 cm of the cup, from 1.35 cm above its top, was too weak for a 5 s transfer with a 105° yaw change, and the cup was already tilted 5.4° (partly along the closing axis, a sign of a poor grip). It slipped out mid-transfer and ended lying on its side, which is far harder to recover than an upright cup. Deeper grasps (jaws over about 4 cm of the cup) used afterwards held B and A securely. Secondary problems cost time and nearly a second cup:
- **A's descent.** A's descent past the rod top was one 3.6 cm move based on a noisy fit. The tracking error put the cup's bottom edge onto the rod top. My correction loop then chased a cup that had pivoted in the grip, instead of stopping at the stall. Later bookkeeping errors added to this: a bottom estimate contaminated by box-top points, a stale command left by a refused preview, and the yaw-free top-down C approach passing over the box edge.
- **Gripper contacts hidden.** I filtered gripper-link contacts out of my collision check. That hid a real jaw-versus-box-edge collision during the C recovery, and I also forgot to reopen the gripper.

What I would do differently:
- Use the deep grasp from the start.
- Keep yaw changes small and transfers slow.
- Descend past the rod top in short steps with a stall check (TCP z above its command), and lift immediately on a stall rather than correcting laterally.
- Measure the cup bottom from the lowest valid circle slice.
- Keep the jaw contacts in path checks over the box.
- Recompute every command from the actual state after a refused preview.
lessons:
Lessons for similar episodes:
- **Check reachability first.** On this PiPER sim, straight-down poses far from the base are unreachable above low heights. Tilted approaches, and even near-horizontal ones, reach much higher.
- **Expect tracking errors.** The arm has a direction-dependent tracking error of 3-7 mm and about 2°. For tolerances near 1 mm, measure the object itself in the world (circle fits on point-cloud slices of the held cylinder worked well when it was near vertical, with residuals of 0.1 mm) and correct in closed loop. Pre-compensating with the TCP error alone is not enough, because orientation errors move a held object's far end.
- **Expect pivoting.** A cylinder held in parallel jaws pivots about the closing axis whenever its end is pushed. The fix is to rotate the gripper about the closing axis by the measured tilt; that restored a 30° tilt to about 1°.
- **Grip deep.** Grip cups over several centimetres, never just the rim region, and avoid large yaw changes with a load.
- **The gripper is binary** (any non-zero command closes it). Plan neighbour clearance with the full 7 cm opening and the real jaw size; my jaw model from wrist depth was more useful than the coarse collision spheres.
- **Singularities:** near q5≈0, Cartesian previews fail even when IK succeeds; a yaw change about the vertical, which keeps a hanging object vertical, finds a path.
- **Guard every descent** with a stall check, and never reuse a command variable a refused preview may have modified.
- **Wrist look pose:** TCP (0.24,0.10,0.22) in the home orientation gives a clear depth view of the crucible floor for verifying placements. Items directly behind the rod are occluded.
